decisions.reason: The message's J_PWR_POWER clause is already fully represented by the candidate's same-message INTRODUCE Event; the signal-interface change requires no additional or corrected candidate Event.
Routing SDA0 and SCL0 through J_PWR_SIGNAL does not change the established cable-length, bus-speed, pull-up resistance, or pull-up-location requirements.
The message assigns D+ and D- to interboard connector pins but does not change the candidate's requirement to provide the native USB data lines.
J_PWR_POWER and J_PWR_SIGNAL are interboard connectors; the source does not alter J_BAT, its three-pin pinout, battery compatibility, or mounting access.
The electrical connector selections and pinouts do not necessarily change the board dimensions, orientation, mounting holes, connector clearance, or spacing constraints.
Assigning 5V_EN to J_PWR_SIGNAL pin 7 records its interboard route but does not change the switched rail's GPIO control, default state, converter, or operating policy.
The source does not change the SK6812 charge-status indication path or the decision not to use a separate charge LED.
The interboard power and signal connector pinouts do not alter battery overcharge, overdischarge, thermal sensing, or thermal protection requirements.
Selecting specific JST connector types does not modify the existing general sourceability and compatible-alternative policy.
Including IRQ and PWRON in the signal pinout does not change the ESP32 clock, sleep, deep-sleep, or wake-source behavior.
Using separate power and signal connectors within the existing three-board design does not change the three-board architecture itself.
